title: About the Microsoft Copilot Readiness Assessment

blocks.text: The inadvertent oversharing of sensitive internal files poses a major security risk, which is further amplified by AI integrations like Microsoft Copilot. Because these tools can expose data from improperly secured files, organizations must implement proactive monitoring and access controls to prevent accidental data exposure.
The Microsoft Copilot Readiness Assessment page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Identify overshared sensitive files within your organization and take appropriate action.
Mitigate risk and ensure secure onboarding for Microsoft Copilot.

blocks.text: The following SaaS applications are supported:

blocks.item: Microsoft SharePoint
Microsoft OneDrive
Microsoft Teams

blocks.text: To ensure successful execution of remediation actions for OneDrive, SharePoint, and Teams, the following prerequisites must be fulfilled:

blocks.item: Ensure your organization's OneDrive, SharePoint, and Teams tenants are successfully onboarded. To learn more, see Adding SaaS Application Tenants.
Define and activate Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies, targeting the onboarded OneDrive, SharePoint, and Teams tenants.

Configure and enable active scanning for the onboarded tenants. This mechanism ensures continuous monitoring of content and activity to detect policy violations defined by your DLP policies, which subsequently triggers the necessary remediation actions. To learn more, see About SaaS Security Scan Configuration.
Onboard Microsoft Information Protection (MIP) labels using either a Zscaler-defined connector or certificate-based authentication. To learn more, see About Microsoft Information Protection Labels.

blocks.heading: About the Microsoft Copilot Readiness Assessment Page

blocks.text: On the Microsoft Copilot Readiness Assessment page (Data Security > DSPM > Workflows > Microsoft Copilot Readiness Assessment), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Filter the report by the following:
Time Range: Choose from Current Day, Current Week, Last 24 Hours, Last 7 Days, Last 15 Days, or Custom.
Application: Choose from one or many of the Microsoft SaaS application tenants: OneDrive, SharePoint, and Teams. The default option is Any.
Gain a comprehensive view of the sensitive assets in your organization:

Total No. of Sensitive Assets: Displays the total number of sensitive assets for the selected SaaS application tenants. A sensitive asset is any document that has either a DLP dictionary, DLP violation, or a DLP engine match. Clicking the displayed value opens the View All Assets page, where you can see detailed information in a tabular format. This data includes the Asset Name, DLP Engine, Tenant, Exposure, Risk, DLP Classification, Internal Collaborators, and External Collaborators.

Sensitive Assets Exposed Org-Wide: Displays the total number of sensitive assets that have an internal shareable link. Clicking the displayed value opens the View All Assets page, where you can see detailed information in a tabular format. This data includes the Asset Name, DLP Engine, Tenant, Exposure, Risk, DLP Classification, Internal Collaborators, and External Collaborators.

Sensitive Assets Exposed with Specific Users: Displays the total number of sensitive assets that have internal collaborators. Clicking the displayed value opens the View All Assets page, where you can see detailed information in a tabular format. This data includes the Asset Name, DLP Engine, Tenant, Exposure, Risk, DLP Classification, Internal Collaborators, and External Collaborators.
View All Assets in Tabular Format

Click to view detailed information in a tabular format. This data includes the Asset Name, DLP Engine, Tenant, Exposure, Risk, DLP Classification, Internal Collaborators, and External Collaborators. In the tabular format, you can also filter by Time Range, Application, and Exposure. When viewing detailed information for the assets, you can apply a remediation action. To apply a remediation action, select a row and choose an option from the Actions drop-down menu:

Apply MIP Label: You can apply a Microsoft Purview Information Protection (formerly Microsoft Information Protection (MIP)) label to Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and PDF files within MIP onboarded tenants.
To apply labels, you must first onboard your MIP labels using certificate-based authentication. To learn more, see About Microsoft Information Protection Labels.

Quarantine to User Root Folder: You can quarantine an incident-reported file to the user's root folder by selecting a Tombstone template used to create a Tombstone file that replaces the quarantined file in its original location.
Remove External Collaborators and Shareable Link: You can revoke the file's public link and remove the external collaborators.
Remove Internal Collaborators and Shareable Link: You can revoke the file's internal link and remove the internal collaborators.
Remove Sharing: You can revoke the sharing permission from a collaborator.
Report Incident: You can report an incident for an asset that triggers an incident.
The following limitations apply for remediation actions:
The maximum batch size for bulk actions is 1,000 assets.
A maximum of 10 bulk remediation jobs can be in progress at any given time.
After you have initiated an action on an asset, you must wait for its completion before applying another action to the same asset.
Bulk remediation action is not supported for assets that were previously quarantined.
Only Report Incident is supported for Microsoft Teams, although other actions remain visible in the menu.
Remediation actions are not supported for Microsoft Teams channels that contain special characters in their names.
3. Asset Exposure
Displays the assets exposed in your organization in the following categories:
Assets Exposed Org-Wide: Displays the percentage of assets selected across the SaaS application tenants which have an internal shareable link.
Assets Exposed Using External Link: Displays the percentage of assets selected across the SaaS application tenants which have an external shareable link.
Assets exposed with >1000 users: Displays the percentage of assets that are exposed to greater than 1,000 users.

Exposure: Displays exposure information in a pie chart and numeric value. Each of the numeric values is clickable, and you can view a drill down of data from Applications > Owners > Assets. You can view information from the following perspectives:
Org-Wide: Displays the total count of assets that have an internal shareable link.
External Link: Displays the total count of assets that have external users or an external shareable link.
Assets Shared With 10-99 Users: Displays the total count of assets that have between 10 and 99 internal collaborators.
Assets Shared With 100-999 Users: Displays the total count of assets that have between 100 and 999 internal collaborators.
Assets Shared With >1000 Users: Display the total count of assets that have greater than 1,000 internal collaborators.
Assets Shared With >=10000 Users: Displays the total count of assets that have greater than or equal to 10,000 internal collaborators.
View All: Click to drill down and further analyze information about assets. To learn more, see Viewing Drilldown of All Assets.
Assets Exposed Org-Wide and Assets Exposed Using External Link options are not supported for MS Teams.
4. Top Risk Assets
Displays the top risk assets exposed in your organization in the following categories:
DLP Violations: Displays the number of assets containing DLP violations.
DLP Incidents: Displays the number of assets containing DLP incidents.
ML Category: Displays the number of assets containing machine learning categories.

View All: Click to view detailed information in a tabular format. This data includes the Asset Name, DLP Engine, Tenant, Exposure, Risk, DLP Classification, Internal Collaborators, and External Collaborators. In the tabular format, you can also filter by Time Range, Application, and Exposure.
